div.head: VI As 1.4
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe þyfðe oft ǽr forworht wære openlice ⁊ to órdale gá ⁊ þar fúl weorðe, þæt hine man slea, buton þa magas oððe se hlaford hine útniman willan be his were ⁊ be fullan ceapgilde ⁊ eac hine on borh gehabban syððan, þæt he ælces yfeles geswice. Gif he eft ofer þæt stalie, agifan þa mágas þonne hine, swa gewyld swa hine ær út æt þam ordale namon, þam gerefan þe þar togebyrige, ⁊ slea man hine on þa þeofwráce. Gif hine þonne hwa forene forstande ⁊ hine geniman wille, ⁊ he wære fúl æt þam ordale, þæt hine man lecgan ne moste, þæt he wære his feores scyldig, buton he cyng gesohte, ⁊ he him his féorh forgifan wolde, eall swa hit ær æt Gréatanléa ⁊ æt Exanceastre ⁊ æt Þunresfelda gecweden wæs.

Et fur qui sepe forisfactus fuerit aperte et ad ordalium eat (uadat) et reus appareat, occidatur nisi cognatio eius (tribus sua) uel dominus redimere uelit eum secundum weram suam et pleno ceapgildo et etiam in plegium habere deinceps, quod ab omni malo cesset (plegiare, quod semper in reliquum cesset a malo). Et si postea furetur, reddat eum cognacio illa iusticiabilem, sicut ante ab ordalio ceperit, preposito, qui ad hoc pertinebit, et occidatur. Si quis obstabit et eum cripere uelit, reum in ordalio, quin occidatur, uitę suę in culpa sit, nisi regem requirat, et ei uitam perdonare uelit (perdonauerit), sicut apud Greatteleiam et Exoniam et apud Þunresfeldam dictum est

⁊ se ðe þyfðe oft ǽr forworht wære openlice ⁊ to órdale gá ⁊ þar fúl weorðe, þæt hine man slea, buton þa magas oððe se hlaford hine útniman willan be his were ⁊ be fullan ceapgilde ⁊ eac hine on borh gehabban syððan, þæt he ælces yfeles geswice. Gif he eft ofer þæt stalie, agifan þa mágas þonne hine swa gewyld swa hine ær út æt þam ordale namon, þam gerefan þe þar togebyrige, ⁊ slea man hine on þa þeofwráce. Gif hine þonne hwa forene forstande ⁊ hine geniman wille, ⁊ he wære fúl æt þam ordale, þæt hine man lecgan ne moste, þæt he wære his feores scyldig, buton he cyng gesohte, ⁊ he him his féorh forgifan wolde, eall swa hit ær æt Gréatanléa ⁊ æt Exanceastre ⁊ æt Þunresfelda gecweden wæs.

Und wer Diebstahls [schon] zuvor oft offenbar überführt gewesen ist und [nun] zum Ordal schreitet und dabei schuldig befunden wird: dass man ihn erschlage, es sei denn, die Verwandten oder der Herr wollen ihn [aus der Haft] herausnehmen gegen Zahlung seines Wergeldes und des vollen Ersatzes [für das Gestohlene] und ausserdem ihn fernerhin unter Verbürgung [dafür] halten, dass er von jeder Missethat abstehe Wenn er wiederum nach diesem stiehlt, dann sollen ihn die Verwandten so gefesselt zurückliefern, wie sie ihn zuvor von dem Ordale [an sich] genommen hatten, an den Vogt, der dort zuständig ist, und erschlage man ihn gemäss der Diebesstrafe. Wenn aber einer für ihn eintritt und ihn [dem Gericht] fortnehmen will, obwohl jener beim Ordal schuldig befunden war, so dass man den [Dieb] nicht hinrichten kann: dass der [Begünstiger] sein Leben verwirkt habe, es sei denn, er suche den König auf, und dieser wolle ihm sein Leben schenken: ganz wie es zuvor zu Greatley und zu Exeter und zu Thundersfield verkündet worden ist.

And whoever has [already] often been openly convicted of theft before and [now] goes to the ordeal and is found guilty there: that he be killed, unless the kinsmen or the lord are willing to take him out [of custody] on payment of his wergild and the full compensation [for the stolen goods], and moreover to keep him thereafter under surety [to the effect] that he will desist from all wrongdoing. If he steals again after this, then the kinsmen are to hand him back, bound just as they had [first] taken him from the ordeal, to the reeve who is responsible there, and let him be killed according to the punishment for thieves. But if anyone intervenes for him and wants to take him away [from the court], although he was found guilty at the ordeal, so that the [thief] cannot be executed: that the [protector] shall have forfeited his life, unless he seeks out the king and the king is willing to grant him his life: just as was proclaimed previously at Greatley and at Exeter and at Thundersfield.

And he who has been frequently and publicly convicted of theft, and who goes to the ordeal and is there proved guilty, shall be slain, unless his kinsmen or his lord will ransom him by the payment of his wergeld and the full value of the [stolen] goods; and in addition, stand surety for him henceforth, that he will desist from every form of crime. If he steals again after this, his kinsmen shall give him back to the reeve to whose jurisdiction the case belongs, in as helpless a condition as he was when they delivered him from the ordeal; and he shall be slain in accordance with the punishment for theft. Further, if anyone stands up for him and wishes to rescue him in order to prevent his being killed, after he has been convicted at the ordeal, he shall forfeit his life unless he appeals to the king, and the king is willing to grant him his life, just as was declared at Grately, and at Exeter, and at Thundersfield.

note.seg: before the bracket Lond; (the bracketed words) the others
nicht ‘Diebstahl begangen hat’. Der Ggs. ist ‘nicht sofort überführbar oder gar handhaft’; u. 9
not ‘has committed theft’. The contrast is ‘not immediately convictable, or even caught in the act’; below 9
Ordal (s. d. Gl 22) allein reinigt Bescholtene
Only the ordeal (see that word in Gl 22) clears men of ill repute
Kerkerstrafe trifft Ordalfällige wenigstens zuerst II 6, 1. Sie ist auch hier laut des utniman hinzuzudenken
Imprisonment is imposed on those who fail in the ordeal, at least at first, II 6, 1. Here too it is to be understood, as the utniman shows
Diese Zeile ist gemeint mit dem Zitat des Greatley-Gesetzes am Schlusse dieses Paragraphen. — Auf diesen Satz bezieht sich VI 9. Vgl. Gl Gefolge 16c
This line is what is meant by the citation of the Greatley law at the end of this paragraph. — VI 9 refers to this sentence. Cf. Gl Gefolge 16c

Die Busse fehlt. Schwerlich, wie Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 136 meint, weil die Gilde, nicht der Bestohlene, den Verbrecher verfolgt. Auch in 7, wo doch Bestohlener die Verfolgung übernimmt, erhält er zwar deren Kosten ersetzt, aber Busse (s. d. Gl 2), obwohl auch da vielleicht nicht immer Leibesstrafe eintrat, ist nicht erwähnt

The compensation is missing. Hardly, as Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 136 thinks, because the gild, and not the man robbed, pursues the criminal. In 7 too, where the man robbed does take over the pursuit, he is indeed reimbursed its costs, but compensation (see that word in Gl 2) is not mentioned, although there too corporal punishment perhaps did not always follow
‘richtbar’ Q, aus Gallolatein, dem Sinne nach richtig, eig. ‘gefangen, um abgeurteilt und ev. hingerichtet werden zu können’
‘justiciable’ Q, from Gallo-Latin, correct in sense, properly ‘captured so that he can be sentenced and possibly executed’
Nicht allein Londons Stadtvogt, sondern ‘den betreffenden Richter’
Not London’s town reeve alone, but ‘the judge concerned’
S. Wb: on S. 165 Z. 3; Toller 746 III 3
See Wb: on p. 165 l. 3; Toller 746 III 3
Wieder wie 1, 2f. strenger als II 1, 5. Vgl. Gl Begünstigung 9ff.
Again, as in 1, 2f., stricter than II 1, 5. Cf. Gl Begünstigung 9ff.
Das Zitat bezieht sich nicht auf die Begnadigung (s. d. Gl 8), sondern das Vorhergehende
The citation refers not to the pardon (see that word in Gl 8), but to what precedes
Wie im Pro ist Faversham nicht erwähnt
As in the Pro, Faversham is not mentioned
Wie dort ist der letzte Reichstag u. 12, 1 nicht erwähnt
As there, the last assembly of the realm, below 12, 1, is not mentioned
Cf. II As. cap. 1 § 4; V As. Preamble § 3; IV As. cap. 6 § 3.
